Summary from the report Not complete yet 14:48

Rorc and Tbx21 knockouts move Th17 genes in opposite directions, while the screen's largest effect, Tgfbr1, is a one-guide Trbv3 population and not a knockout effect. The positive control holds mainly on the Tbx21 side inside Th17 states t11-tbx21-il17a-within-S02, Tgfbr1 is traced to guide 1 in NTN2 t10-tgfbr1-clone, and the Socs1, Traf6 and Il17a edges stay candidates t7-F9-Il17a-Il1r1-guide-split.

  1. Rorc and Tbx21 knockouts move the Th17 genes in opposite directions in kidney inflammation and colitis
  2. The largest effect in the screen, Tgfbr1, is a Trbv3-dominant population carried mainly by one guide in one experiment, not a knockout effect
  3. Socs1, Traf6, Jak2 and Il17a loss are candidate regulators of the Th17 genes; no leg is established, and each is weak or limited to one model

Result 1, in the report, 15:07, version 5

Rorc and Tbx21 knockouts move the Th17 genes in opposite directions in kidney inflammation and colitis

Observation: Rorc knockout lowers Il17a (-1.97) and Il23r (-1.99), and Tbx21 knockout raises Il17a (+1.73) and Il23r (+1.04), in the same 10 captures against other targets' cells and in single-guide cells1,2. The two have opposite sign in 18 of 20 target-capture comparisons3. Tbx21 raises Il23r in 3 of 5 guides and Rorc lowers it in 3 of 5, both beyond the control-guide groups4,5. As programmes, the IL-23 score rises in Tbx21 cells (+0.19, 4 of 5 guides) and falls in Rorc cells (-0.098, 4 of 5 guides)6,7; the T-bet score falls in Tbx21 cells (-0.12, 5 of 5 guides) and rises in Rorc cells (+0.099, 3 of 5 guides)8,9. Within state S02 the Tbx21 side holds: Tbx21 cells raise Il17a (+2.39) and Il23r (+0.92)10. The Rorc side is thinner: in S02 only Il17a falls (-1.74, q 0.036, 131 cells), and Il23r and Ccr6 do not pass11. Rorc does not raise Ifng or Cxcr3 within states, and Tbx21 loss lowers them, so the Rorc-raises-T-bet reading is not supported at gene level12.

Inference: the Tbx21 effect on Th17 genes is direct and persists within states; Rorc's opposite effect is real on Il17a but weaker, and the opposition concerns Il17a, Il23r and Ccr6, not the full profile (whole-profile r -0.25)3.

Limits: Rorc guides 2 and 5 and Tbx21 guide 4 are weak, and the two disease models are not compared by test2.

Result 2, in the report, 15:20, version 4

The largest effect in the screen, Tgfbr1, is a Trbv3-dominant population carried mainly by one guide in one experiment, not a knockout effect

Tgfbr1 is the only target past its control-guide line, with an e-distance of 1.342. The signal comes almost entirely from guide 1 in the NTN2 experiment.1 In each of the three NTN2 captures, 94% to 96% of guide-1 cells with a Trbv transcript (961, 680 and 871 cells) have Trbv3 dominant. Same-capture controls show 16% to 26%, and Tgfbr1's other guides 2% to 5%.1 Guide 1 barely lowers Tgfbr1 itself (own gene -0.07), so a knockout is not the likely cause.1 The other guides' own-gene changes are -1.32 (guide 2), -0.83 (guide 3), -0.69 (guide 4) and +0.39 (guide 5); guides 2 and 4 are marked not measurable.1 The Trbv3 skew is not confined to guide 1: in one colitis capture, 46% of the other Tgfbr1 guides' 110 cells are Trbv3 dominant, against 4% of controls.1

Inference: the shift is mainly guide 1's composition, a population enriched in one transferred pool, rather than a within-state change.3

Limits: the three NTN2 captures probably share one pool, so they are not independent replicates; clonality rests on a Trbv proxy with no CDR3 read.1 A repeat needs a new capture or CDR3 data, which this design lacks.1

Socs1, Traf6, Jak2 and Il17a loss are candidate regulators of the Th17 genes; no leg is established, and each is weak or limited to one model

Observation: Socs1 knockout lowers Il17a (-1.4), Il17f and Ccr6 pooled, 3 of 5 guides, 144 genes changed against a control-guide 95th percentile of 3.71. Its Th17 score falls (-0.051, 3 of 5 guides) but the Wilcoxon test on that score does not agree (+0.003)4. Socs1 also raises the T-bet score (+0.077, 3 of 5 guides)6. Jak2 knockout lowers Tbx21 (-0.7, 5 of 5 guides) in the nephritis captures only3. Il17a, Ahr, Myd88 and Traf6 knockouts raise Il1r1 (about +0.4 each) but only 2 to 3 of 5 guides agree, and Il17a guides 3 to 5 go the other way2. Traf6 raises the IL-23 score (+0.093, 4 of 5 guides) though its own transcript is not lowered5.

Inference: Jak2 acting on Tbx21 and Socs1 restraining the Th17 programme fit known cytokine signalling, but the Il1r1 edge and the Traf6 effect lack own-gene knockdown, so they are candidates, not established edges2,5.

Next question: do these hold with the Tgfbr1 guide-1 clone removed?

Finding t10-tgfbr1-clone, description, recorded 14:29, reworded 15:19

Tgfbr1's headline signal is a Trbv3-dominant population carried mainly by guide 1 in NTN2

Tgfbr1's headline signal is a Trbv3-dominant population carried mainly by guide 1 in NTN2, not a knockout effect: in each of the 3 NTN2 captures 94% to 96% of guide-1 cells with a Trbv transcript (961, 680 and 871 cells) have Trbv3 dominant, against 16% to 26% of same-capture controls and 2% to 5% of Tgfbr1's other guides. Guide 1 barely lowers Tgfbr1 itself (own gene -0.07, 2,788 cells); the other guides' own-gene changes are -1.32 (guide 2, 107 cells), -0.83 (guide 3, 527), -0.69 (guide 4, 107) and +0.39 (guide 5, 255), with guides 2 and 4 marked not measurable by the run. The Trbv3 shift is not confined to guide 1: in one colitis capture (Th17-1) 46% of the other Tgfbr1 guides' 110 cells are Trbv3 dominant, against 4% of controls. The three NTN2 captures probably share one transferred pool, so they are not independent replicates; clonality is a Trbv proxy, with no CDR3 read.

No checks recordedRuns 2Concerns 1: narrows the findingRevised 2×

Context and references

Prior knowledge: A same-V-gene population dominating one guide in one capture is what a single expanded T-cell clone looks like; Trbv usage is only a proxy for clonotype here (no CDR3 sequence). (prior knowledge)

The skeptic's check

Clonality read from Trbv alone, with no CDR3 Raised a concern (d-t10-clone)

Concerns

"Clonal expansion" rests on a dominant Trbv gene (Trbv3 in 96%) among cells carrying a Trbv transcript. Many clones share a Trbv, and only the V segment is used, with no CDR3. A guide-1-specific Trbv3-skewed population (a transduction or sorting bottleneck) is not separated from true clonality. Trbv3 is also common in NTN2 controls (22%). (d-t10-clone, 14:32, raised by the skeptic)
Would change the conclusion: If CDR3 clonotype calls show few distinct clonotypes in guide-1 NTN2 cells, "clone" stands. If many share Trbv3, reword to a Trbv3-skewed population.
14:33
Narrows the findingThe claim is narrowed to 'a Trbv3-dominant expansion carried by one guide in one experiment'; no CDR3 was read, so clonality is a proxy and is stated as a limit of the readout.

Finding f5, description, recorded 14:09

The Tgfbr1 signature is one guide in one experiment: in NTN2

The Tgfbr1 signature is one guide in one experiment: in NTN2 (3 captures) Tgfbr1 cells leave the Th17-core states for a TCR-V-high state S14 (58% vs 1.9% in controls; total variation 0.83, above the control-group maximum 0.57), carried by gRNA_Tgfbr1_1 (2,646 cells, TV 0.87; guide 5 with 110 cells looks like controls); guide 1 also holds 94% of Tgfbr1 cells in the NTN2 captures against about 30% in controls, so the lower Il17a/Rorc/Ccr6 there mostly reflects composition (within S12 and S17, Il17a matches controls) and a possibly clonal expansion; NTN1 (TV 0.17) and colitis (TV 0.09) stay inside the control range

Rorc, Irf4, Jak1 and Il7r do not deplete Th17 states: in NTN2 they have 27 to 110 cells (too few); in NTN1 Irf4 and Rorc move within the control range, with Irf4 TV 0.39 vs control max 0.49, and their Th17-core share (S02, S06, S07) is similar to the other targets. The skeptic's check

Read run0036-cc31aa. It pools cells per experiment with no capture units, no test and no checks. In NTN2 and colitis the other targets (Tgfbr1, Tgfbr2, Socs1) also lower Il17a by about as much as Rorc, which points to a baseline or common-response offset. Raised a concern (d1)

Concerns

run0036-cc31aa pools cells per experiment (cells as observations, no capture-level units; NTN2 control n=904, colitis control n=598) against control-guide cells. Every target in NTN2 and colitis is lowered on Il17a (NTN2 Il17a: Tgfbr1 -0.64, Tgfbr2 -0.50, Socs1 -0.44, against Rorc -0.61; colitis Socs1 -0.76). Rorc's -0.61 in NTN2 is therefore no different from non-Th17 targets, and the Tbx21 rise may be partly a baseline offset between control-guide and perturbed cells, or a common response of perturbed cells. Only NTN1 separates Rorc from the others (Rorc -0.71, Tgfbr1 -0.10, Tgfbr2 -0.14). The finding says the positive control "repeats", but no per-experiment test or unit count backs it. (d1, 13:51, raised by the skeptic)
Would change the conclusion: Rerun Rorc and Tbx21 per experiment with the reference as other targets (same blocks, reference other_targets), and with captures as units where an experiment has more than 2. If Rorc stays below and Tbx21 above the other targets in each experiment, f4 stands. If Rorc is indistinguishable from Tgfbr1, Tgfbr2 and Socs1 in NTN2 and colitis, narrow f4 to NTN1 and treat the others as untested.

The Tbx21 wording "the opposite of Rorc knockout" rests on Il17a, Ccr6 and Il23r, while the profile correlation is only r -0.25, which is weak for "opposite". Read the lead (edgeR by capture, 10 captures, q 0.0011), the five guides alone, the field's other tests (Wilcoxon, DESeq2) and the control-guide calibration. Concerns

Rorc's guides do not carry the effect evenly. Rorc_1 is not significant (q 0.071, own gene -0.82), Rorc_5 is weak (-0.79), and Rorc_3 gives -4.03 from 262 cells, 137 of them in a single capture (Colitis_2_23_2_Th17-2). Its own gene reads -0.26 to -1.36 per guide, which for knockout says little (PF7). The pooled -1.97 therefore leans on Rorc_3 and Rorc_4. The captures (units) differ per guide, so the guide estimates are not from the same units. Rorc cells could also be a shifted mix of Th17 and non-Th17 states, not a lower Il17a within cells. What the targets' changed genes are: Tgfbr1 217, Tbx21 314, Rorc 67, Socs1 144, Traf6 88 genes. Read them as programmes and published Th17 sets (pathogenic vs. regulatory, IL-23, TGF-beta, T-bet/IFNg). explained (t6)

Closed because: Set-level programme reads of the five targets' changed genes against control guides, by disease model apart, with own genes removed. Five targets move a Th17 programme past its control line: Tbx21 (IL-23/Th17 up, T-bet/IFN-g down), Rorc (IL-23 down, T-bet up), Socs1 (T-bet up, IL-23 down), Traf6 (IL-23 and non-pathogenic up), Tgfbr1 (TGF-b response down in NTN only; proliferation up, guide-dependent). Hallmark ORA and collectri ULM give the same axis (IFN-g/IL2-STAT5 up for Socs1 and Rorc; E2F/MYC activity for Tgfbr1, Traf6, Socs1). Caveats: Tgfbr1 proliferation is carried by guide 1 (2788 of 3784 cells), and control-group calibration beyond the 95th percentile is required for each call.

Closed because: f1 and f2 hold on single-guide cells: the Rorc and Tbx21 gene runs on label-defined single-guide cells reproduce their values exactly (Il17a -1.97 and +1.73). Guide strength qualifies f2 but does not contradict it: Il17a and Ccr6 rise in the three Tbx21 guides with knockdown, and the strongest-knockdown Tbx21 guide is not the strongest effect; the one guide with no knockdown (guide 4, 382 cells) is flat. Rorc own gene -1.31 is guide 4 only; Tbx21 own gene -1.31 in the dose view is guide 5 (the own-gene log2 of the two strongest guides is -1.0 to -1.1 in the efficacy run). Guide-pair agreement is 0.24 within target against -0.03 across targets.

The research lead

The lead reads the record as a whole, judges whether the results make a story, and opens the threads for what is missing. Its reviews, the latest first.

Review 3 Complete (14:48)

The screen's only target past its control-guide line, Tgfbr1 (e-distance 1.34 vs 0.76), is a guide-1, NTN2 composition and clonal-state shift, not a knockout effect (r1, r2). The clearest real structure is the Rorc versus Tbx21 opposition on Th17 genes, which holds with the other-targets reference and in single-guide cells. Socs1, Traf6 and Il17a edges are candidates, narrowed in r3 by the guide and own-gene doubts. The main line reached level 3 (where it holds). The within-state test of Rorc/Tbx21 (t11) is still open and goes in the report as pending. Complete is proposed because the remaining questions need new guides or captures the design lacks.

Main line: kept. Keep the line at t10. It explained the strongest observation, Tgfbr1, as clonal composition. Nothing else beats it.

Review 2 Not complete yet (14:28)

The screen's only target past its control-guide line is Tgfbr1, but states, guides and captures show that signal to be mostly one guide in one experiment (NTN2, state S14, composition), so it is a technical or clonal outlier, not a clean hit. The robust biology is Rorc lowering and Tbx21 raising Il17a, Il23r and Ccr6, which holds against other targets, per capture and on single-guide cells. It is narrowed to direction, and Rorc/Socs1 also raise the T-bet programme. The main line reached level 3 (where it holds) and partly level 5. The within-state test of the Rorc/Tbx21 opposition (t11) and the clone/guide test of Tgfbr1 (t10) are still open, no result has been proposed, and t6 and t7 have not ended. The protein readout is limited because five of twelve NTN units have all-zero antibody counts.

Review 1 Not complete yet (13:46)

The screen (28 targets, 158k in-vivo cells, 12 units, NTN and colitis apart) has one target past its control-guide line, Tgfbr1 (e-distance 1.34 vs 0.76, 217 genes), and two Th17 positive controls, Rorc KO down and Tbx21 KO up on Il17a, Il23r and Ccr6 (f1, f2), on a low-reproducibility base (replicate r 0.05, weak guide agreement, 49% multi-guide cells, Rorc itself below its line at 0.21 vs 1.40). The main line is at level 1 to 2: Tgfbr1 copies the Rorc/Socs1 signature in panel e, and 74% of its cells are in NTN_2_23_1 captures, so capture, clone or guide must be ruled out (t2) before a structure is claimed. The shared-profile set alike:Ahr+27 looks NTN-specific (Tgfbr1-Tgfbr2 0.84 NTN vs 0.07 colitis) and the colitis control reference is sparse (598 cells), so t3 (other_targets fork), t4 (single-guide and dose check) and t5 (the set) come before f1 and f2 support a Th17/Th1 axis. Stopped lines without a route beyond these: replicate agreement (too few cells per capture; routes t2 and t4), multi-guide cells (confounded by the design; route t4). Programmes, states, target-on-target and protein readouts are with workers (t6 to t9), and the states survey is still running.

from pertura.cell_table import retype
import anndata as ad, re
cap=[v for v in ad.read_h5ad(f"{cell_tables}/NTN_2_23_1_Th17-1.h5ad").var_names if v.endswith('_capture')]
low={c.lower():c for c in cap}
special={'cd40l':'cd40lg','sykb':'syk','tgfrb2':'tgfbr2'}
def m(n):
    b=n[len('gRNA_'):-len('_gene')]; g,i=b.rsplit('_',1)
    g=g.lower().replace('-','')
    g=special.get(g,g)
    return low.get(f"grna_{g}_{i}_capture")
samples=["NTN_1_19_5","NTN_1_19_9_1","NTN_1_19_9_2","NTN_1_19_23_1","NTN_1_19_23_2"]
for s in samples:
    a=ad.read_h5ad(f"{cell_tables}/{s}.h5ad")
    mp={n:m(n) for n in a.var_names if n.startswith('gRNA') and n.endswith('_gene')}
    bad=[k for k,v in mp.items() if v is None]
    print(s,len(mp),bad, len(set(mp.values())))
    if not bad: print(retype(cell_tables,s,mp))
for s in ["NTN_2_23_1_Control","NTN_2_23_1_Th17-1","NTN_2_23_1_Th17-2","NTN_2_23_1_Th17-3","Colitis_2_23_2_Control","Colitis_2_23_2_Th17-1","Colitis_2_23_2_Th17-2"]:
    a=ad.read_h5ad(f"{cell_tables}/{s}.h5ad")
    gl=[n for n in a.var_names[(a.var.feature_types=='Gene Expression').values] if n.startswith('gRNA') and n.endswith('_gene')]
    print(s,len(gl))
    print(retype(cell_tables,s,{n:m(n) for n in gl},feature_type="Guide read in the expression"))

import anndata as ad
S=["NTN_1_19_5","NTN_1_19_9_1","NTN_1_19_9_2","NTN_1_19_23_1","NTN_1_19_23_2","NTN_2_23_1_Control","NTN_2_23_1_Th17-1","NTN_2_23_1_Th17-2","NTN_2_23_1_Th17-3","Colitis_2_23_2_Control","Colitis_2_23_2_Th17-1","Colitis_2_23_2_Th17-2"]
mouse={"NTN_1_19_5":"NTN1_mouse5","NTN_1_19_9_1":"NTN1_mouse9","NTN_1_19_9_2":"NTN1_mouse9","NTN_1_19_23_1":"NTN1_mouse23","NTN_1_19_23_2":"NTN1_mouse23"}
for s in S[5:]: mouse[s]=s
def idx(s): return ad.read_h5ad(f"{cell_tables}/{s}.h5ad",backed='r').obs_names
import pandas as pd
print(annotate(cell_tables,"mouse",{s:pd.Series(mouse[s],index=idx(s)) for s in S},made_by=f"run:{run_id}",note="NTN_1_19 samples named <exp>_<year>_<mouse>[_lane]: 9_1/9_2 and 23_1/23_2 read as two channels of one mouse (same sex by XIST); sample name = unit elsewhere. Inferred from names."))
dis={s:("colitis" if s.startswith("Colitis") else "nephrotoxic_nephritis") for s in S}
print(annotate(cell_tables,"disease_model",dis,made_by=f"run:{run_id}",note="GEO treatment characteristic: crescentic glomerulonephritis (kidney) vs experimental colitis (intestine)"))

(folder, column, values, made_by='', note='')
Write a column into the cells of the samples' tables, as the agent reads each cell's unit or condition
    (docs/adr/0041, step 4): values is {sample: the cells' values}, each a Series indexed by the table's barcodes, a
    list in the table's cell order, or one value for every cell of the sample (a condition given by sample); a cell
    the values do not name gets none (''). Each distinct value is a unit or level of its own: a cell that belongs to
    none (its donor or mouse not told) is left without a value, which the build reads as no unit, never a word such as
    'unassigned', which would become a unit (GSE190604: a third "donor" of unassigned cells). The tables are rewritten
    in place, and the column noted in the manifest with who wrote it and how many cells have no value. Returns {ok,
    problems, column, samples: {name: {cells, without_value}}, values: the distinct values, up to 50, cells_per_value,
    read_as}.

import numpy as np, pandas as pd, scipy.sparse as sp, re
a=pt.screen().adata
o=a.obs
print(o.condition.value_counts().to_dict(), o.label_after_qc.value_counts().head(5).to_dict())
X=a.X if sp.issparse(a.X) else sp.csr_matrix(a.X)
lab=o.label_after_qc.values
keep=np.isin(lab,[l for l in pd.unique(lab) if l not in ('none','multi','failed','') and pd.notna(l)])
genes=np.array(a.var_names)
tr=np.array([bool(re.match(r'^(Tr[abdg][vjc]|Tcrg|Trav|Trbv)',g)) for g in genes])
print(tr.sum())
# normalise
tot=np.asarray(X.sum(1)).ravel()
res={}
for cond in ['nephrotoxic_nephritis','colitis']:
    m=(o.condition.values==cond)&keep
    idx=np.where(m)[0]
    Xs=X[idx]; t=tot[idx]
    Xn=sp.diags(1e4/np.maximum(t,1))@Xs; Xn=Xn.tocsr(); Xn.data=np.log1p(Xn.data)
    l=lab[idx]
    expr=np.asarray(Xn.mean(0)).ravel(); sel=expr>0.05
    ctrl=Xn[l=='control'].mean(0).A1
    prof={}
    for g in set(l)-{'control'}:
        k=l==g
        if k.sum()>=30: prof[g]=Xn[k].mean(0).A1-ctrl
    P=pd.DataFrame(prof,index=genes)
    res[cond]=(P,sel,(l=='control').sum(),{g:int((l==g).sum()) for g in P.columns})
    for name,mask in [('all',sel),('noTR',sel&~tr)]:
        C=P[mask].corr(); iu=np.triu_indices(len(C),1)
        print(cond,name,'mean pair r',round(float(np.nanmean(C.values[iu])),3))
    C=P[sel&~tr].corr()
    print(cond,'noTR pairs:',{p:round(C.loc[p[0],p[1]],2) for p in [('Tgfbr1','Tgfbr2'),('Il17a','Traf6'),('Il17a','Nfatc2'),('Jak2','Myd88'),('Tbx21','Jak2')] if p[0] in C and p[1] in C})
    C=P[sel].corr()
    print(cond,'all pairs:',{p:round(C.loc[p[0],p[1]],2) for p in [('Tgfbr1','Tgfbr2'),('Il17a','Traf6'),('Il17a','Nfatc2'),('Jak2','Myd88'),('Tbx21','Jak2')] if p[0] in C and p[1] in C})
    print(cond,'ctrl cells',res[cond][2], 'targets',len(P.columns))

Code
X=a.X; genes=np.array(a.var_names)
if not sp.issparse(X): X=sp.csr_matrix(X)
tot=np.asarray(X.sum(1)).ravel(); 
def prof(idx):
    m=np.asarray(X[idx].sum(0)).ravel(); return np.log1p(m/m.sum()*1e4)
gi={g:i for i,g in enumerate(genes)}
th=['Il17a','Il23r','Ccr6','Rorc','Il1r1','Stat3']
lab=o.label_after_qc.values; unit=o.unit.values
rows=[];P={}
for u in sorted(set(unit[lab=='Tgfbr1'])):
    t=np.where((lab=='Tgfbr1')&(unit==u))[0]; c=np.where((lab=='control')&(unit==u))[0]
    if len(c)<30: rows.append((u,len(t),len(c))+(np.nan,)*len(th)); continue
    d=prof(t)-prof(c); P[u]=d
    rows.append((u,len(t),len(c))+tuple(round(d[gi[g]],2) for g in th))
df=pd.DataFrame(rows,columns=['capture','n_Tgfbr1','n_ctrl']+th); print(df.to_string())
# correlation of each capture's profile with the mean of the others, expressed genes
expr=np.asarray(X.sum(0)).ravel()>200
import itertools
us=list(P); 
for u in us:
    oth=np.mean([P[v] for v in us if v!=u],axis=0); print(u, round(np.corrcoef(P[u][expr],oth[expr])[0,1],2))

depth-matched target shift profiles per disease model (fixed dense conversion), saved to the notebook folder

colitis 28 targets; control cells 598; nephrotoxic_nephritis 28 targets; control cells 3822; saved

Why: t5: remove depth by matching control cells to each target's UMI distribution, then re-correlate the target profiles

Code
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, scipy.sparse as sp, pickle, os
a = pt.screen().adata
ln = pt.screen().lognorm
lab = a.obs['label_after_qc'].astype(str).values
cond = a.obs['condition'].astype(str).values
umi = np.log10(a.obs['umis'].astype(float).values+1)
bins = np.quantile(umi, np.linspace(0,1,21))
bin_id = np.clip(np.searchsorted(bins, umi, side='right')-1, 0, 19)
res = {}; raw = {}; nct = {}
for c in ['colitis','nephrotoxic_nephritis']:
    idx_c = np.where((cond==c)&(lab=='control'))[0]
    X_c = ln[idx_c]
    mc_raw = np.asarray(X_c.mean(axis=0)).ravel()
    targets = [t for t in np.unique(lab[(cond==c)]) if t not in ['none','multi','failed QC','control'] and (lab[(cond==c)]==t).sum()>=10]
    prof = {}; rawp = {}
    for t in targets:
        it = np.where((cond==c)&(lab==t))[0]
        bt = pd.Series(bin_id[it]).value_counts(normalize=True)
        w = np.zeros(len(idx_c))
        for b, frac in bt.items():
            sel = bin_id[idx_c]==b
            if sel.sum()>0:
                w[sel] = frac/sel.sum()
        w = w/w.sum()
        mt = np.asarray(ln[it].mean(axis=0)).ravel()
        mc = np.asarray((sp.csr_matrix(w[None,:]) @ X_c).todense()).ravel()
        prof[t] = mt - mc
        rawp[t] = mt - mc_raw
    res[c] = pd.DataFrame(prof); raw[c] = pd.DataFrame(rawp)
    nct[c] = len(idx_c)
    print(c, len(targets), 'targets; control cells', len(idx_c))
pickle.dump({'matched':res,'raw':raw,'nctrl':nct}, open(os.path.join(os.getcwd(),'t5_profiles.pkl'),'wb'))
print('saved')

Why: t5: test whether the NTN shared profile is a unit-level or technical shift shared by every target-labelled cell

Code
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, scipy.sparse as sp, pickle, os
a = pt.screen().adata
ln = pt.screen().lognorm
lab = a.obs['label_after_qc'].astype(str).values
cond = a.obs['condition'].astype(str).values
unit = a.obs['unit'].astype(str).values
genes = np.array(a.var_names)
res = {}
for c in ['colitis','nephrotoxic_nephritis']:
    targets = [t for t in np.unique(lab[(cond==c)]) if t not in ['none','multi','failed QC','control'] and (lab[(cond==c)]==t).sum()>=10]
    prof = {}
    for t in targets:
        it = np.where((cond==c)&(lab==t))[0]
        mt_u = pd.Series(unit[it]).value_counts(normalize=True)
        mt = np.asarray(ln[it].mean(axis=0)).ravel()
        mc = np.zeros_like(mt); tot=0
        for u,frac in mt_u.items():
            ic = np.where((cond==c)&(lab=='control')&(unit==u))[0]
            if len(ic)==0: continue
            mc += frac*np.asarray(ln[ic].mean(axis=0)).ravel()
            tot += frac
        prof[t] = (mt - mc/ tot)
    P = pd.DataFrame(prof, index=genes)
    res[c]=P
pickle.dump(res, open(os.path.join(os.getcwd(),'t5_unitmatched.pkl'),'wb'))
for c in res:
    P = res[c]
    v = P.var(axis=1)
    P2 = P.loc[v.sort_values(ascending=False).index[:2000]]
    C = P2.corr()
    pairs = [('Tgfbr1','Tgfbr2'),('Jak2','Myd88'),('Il17a','Traf6'),('Ahr','Il17a')]
    print(c, {f'{x}-{y}': round(C.loc[x,y],2) for x,y in pairs if x in C.index and y in C.columns}, 'mean offdiag', round(C.values[np.triu_indices(C.shape[0],1)].mean(),3))
    m = P.mean(axis=1).sort_values()
    print(c,'mean shift top down', list(m.index[:15]))
    print(c,'mean shift top up', list(m.index[-15:][::-1]))
    mt_genes = [g for g in genes if g.startswith('mt-')]
    rb = [g for g in genes if g.startswith(('Rpl','Rps'))]
    print(c,'mean shift mito', round(m[mt_genes].mean(),3), 'ribo', round(m[rb].mean(),3), 'overall', round(m.mean(),3))

import numpy as np, pandas as pd
a = pt.screen().adata; o = a.obs; g = o['guides'].astype(str); ln = pt.screen().lognorm; genes=list(a.var_names)
ctrl = (o['label']=='control').values
out=[]
for t in ['Rorc','Tbx21']:
    j = genes.index(t); x = np.asarray(ln[:, j].todense()).ravel()
    s = (o['label']==t).values
    # single-guide cells by guide id
    gg = g.values
    sg = pd.Series(np.where(s, gg, ''), index=o.index)
    for gid in sorted(set(gg[s])):
        m = s & (gg==gid)
        if m.sum()>=20:
            out.append((t,'single',gid,m.sum(), round(x[m].mean(),3), round(x[ctrl].mean(),3)))

import numpy as np, pandas as pd

a = pt.screen().adata; o = a.obs; g = o['guides'].astype(str).values; ln = pt.screen().lognorm; genes=list(a.var_names)

X = {q: np.asarray(ln[:, genes.index(q)].todense()).ravel() for q in genesq}
def row(name, m, t):
    res=[name, int(m.sum())]
    for q in ['Il17a','Ccr6','Il23r']:
        v=X[q][m]; c=X[q][ctrl]
        d=v.mean()-c.mean()
        p=stats.mannwhitneyu(v,c).pvalue if m.sum()>=10 else np.nan
        res += [q, round(d,3), '%.1e'%p]
    return res
rows=[]
s_ctrl=ctrl
for t in ['Rorc','Tbx21']:
    own=(o['label']==t).values
    for gid in sorted(set(g[own])):
        m = own & (g==gid)
        if m.sum()>=20: rows.append(row(f'{t} single {gid}', m, t))
    mt = ((o['label']=='multi') & pd.Series(g).str.contains(f'gRNA_{t}_').values)
    if t=='Tbx21':
        rows.append(row('Tbx21 multi with Cd40lg_2', mt & pd.Series(g).str.contains('gRNA_Cd40lg_2').values, t))
        rows.append(row('Tbx21 multi without Cd40lg_2', mt & ~pd.Series(g).str.contains('gRNA_Cd40lg_2').values, t))
    else:
        rows.append(row('Rorc multi (all)', mt, t))
rows.append(['Control cells', int(ctrl.sum())])
df=pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(df.to_string())

import numpy as np, pandas as pd, scipy.sparse as sp, re
a = pt.screen().adata
ln = pt.screen().lognorm
genes = np.array(a.var_names)
lab = a.obs['label_after_qc'].astype(str).values
cond = a.obs['condition'].astype(str).values
unit = a.obs['unit'].astype(str).values
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
tcr = re.compile(r'^(Tr[abgd][vjc]|Trbc|Trac|Trgc|Trdc|Tcrg-|Trgv|Trdv)')
keepg = np.array([not bool(tcr.match(g)) for g in genes])
c='nephrotoxic_nephritis'
targets = ['Tgfbr1','Tgfbr2','Jak2','Myd88','Ccr6','Il17a','Traf6','Ahr','Irf4','Cd40lg']
allc = np.where((cond==c)&(lab=='control'))[0]
def profiles(ctrl_idx):
    prof={}
    for t in targets:
        it = np.where((cond==c)&(lab==t))[0]
        mt_u = pd.Series(unit[it]).value_counts(normalize=True)
        mt = np.asarray(ln[it].mean(axis=0)).ravel()
        mc=np.zeros_like(mt); tot=0
        for u,frac in mt_u.items():
            ic = ctrl_idx[unit[ctrl_idx]==u]
            if len(ic)==0: continue
            mc += frac*np.asarray(ln[ic].mean(axis=0)).ravel(); tot+=frac
        prof[t]=(mt-mc/tot)[keepg]
    return pd.DataFrame(prof)
def summ(P):
    v=P.var(axis=1); P2=P.loc[v.sort_values(ascending=False).index[:2000]]
    C=P2.corr()
    return {x+'-'+y: round(C.loc[x,y],2) for x,y in [('Tgfbr1','Tgfbr2'),('Jak2','Myd88'),('Ccr6','Tgfbr2'),('Ahr','Il17a'),('Irf4','Cd40lg')]}, round(C.values[np.triu_indices(C.shape[0],1)].mean(),3)
full = profiles(allc)
print('all NTN controls (3822):', summ(full))
# subsample to 598 controls, 5 draws
for k in range(3):
    sub = rng.choice(allc, size=598, replace=False)
    print('subsample 598 draw',k, summ(profiles(sub)))

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
pd.set_option('display.width',250); pd.set_option('display.max_rows',400)
df = pt.load("20261114T140122-C-programs-f84809:result")
df['sig']=df.q<0.05
s = df.groupby(['condition','target']).agg(n_sig=('sig','sum'), n_up=('effect',lambda x: ((x>0)&(df.loc[x.index,'sig'])).sum()), n_dn=('effect',lambda x: ((x<0)&(df.loc[x.index,'sig'])).sum()))
print(s)
for (c,t),g in df[df.sig].groupby(['condition','target']):
    g=g.sort_values('effect',key=abs,ascending=False)
    print(c,t, [(r.score.replace('_TotalSeqC',''), round(r.effect,3), round(r.q,4) if r.q>1e-10 else '<1e-10') for r in g.head(14).itertuples()])
print(df[['cells','reference_cells','samples','target_samples']].drop_duplicates().to_string())

Why: name states and split the composition by experiment

Code
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, scipy.sparse as sp
a = pt.screen().adata
cs = pt.load('20261114T134310-C-states_and_composition-b254f4:cell_states').set_index('barcode')
o = a.obs.copy()
o['state'] = cs['state'].reindex(o.index).values
o['exp'] = np.where(o['unit'].str.startswith('NTN_2'),'NTN2',np.where(o['unit'].str.startswith('NTN_1'),'NTN1','Colitis'))
X = a.X
genes = ['Cd4','Cd8a','Foxp3','Rorc','Il17a','Ccr6','Il23r','Irf4','Il7r','Jak1','Tgfbr1','Mki67','Top2a','Ccnb2','Trbv3','Trav6-1','Il12rb2','Ifit1','Itk','Cd3e','Ptprc','Cd19','Itgam','Fcer1g','Il2ra','Tbx21','Gzmb','Ifng']
genes=[g for g in genes if g in a.var_names]
idx = {g: a.var_names.get_loc(g) for g in genes}
Xg = X[:, [idx[g] for g in genes]]
Xg = Xg.toarray() if sp.issparse(Xg) else np.asarray(Xg)
df = pd.DataFrame(Xg>0, columns=genes, index=o.index)
df['state']=o['state'].values
frac = df.groupby('state').mean().round(2)
n = df.groupby('state').size()
frac['n']=n
pd.set_option('display.width',250); pd.set_option('display.max_columns',40)

import numpy as np, pandas as pd
a = pt.screen().adata
cs = pt.load('20261114T134310-C-states_and_composition-b254f4:cell_states').set_index('barcode')
o = a.obs.copy()
o['state'] = cs['state'].reindex(o.index).values
o['exp'] = np.where(o['unit'].str.startswith('NTN_2'),'NTN2',np.where(o['unit'].str.startswith('NTN_1'),'NTN1','Colitis'))
o = o[o['label_after_qc']!='failed QC']
ctrl = o[o['label_after_qc']=='control']
rows=[]
for e in ['NTN2','NTN1','Colitis']:
    c = ctrl[ctrl.exp==e]
    cshare = c['state'].value_counts(normalize=True)
    for t in sorted(o['label_after_qc'].unique()):
        if t in ('control','none','multi','failed QC'): continue
        tt = o[(o.label_after_qc==t)&(o.exp==e)]
        if len(tt)<10: continue
        ts = tt['state'].value_counts(normalize=True)
        for s in sorted(set(cshare.index)|set(ts.index)):
            rows.append(dict(exp=e,target=t,state=s,n=len(tt),share=ts.get(s,0),ctrl=cshare.get(s,0),ctrl_n=len(c)))
d = pd.DataFrame(rows); d['diff']=d.share-d.ctrl
d.to_pickle('/data/pertura/workspace/t9_shares.pkl') if False else None
pt.save_table('t9_shares_by_exp', d)
pd.set_option('display.width',250)
# Tgfbr1 table
for e in ['NTN2','NTN1','Colitis']:
    sub = d[(d.exp==e)&(d.target=='Tgfbr1')].set_index('state')[['n','share','ctrl','diff']].round(3)
    print(e, 'Tgfbr1 n', sub.n.iloc[0] if len(sub) else 0, 'ctrl n', ctrl[ctrl.exp==e].shape[0])
    print(sub.T.to_string())
print(o[o.label_after_qc=='Tgfbr1'].exp.value_counts())

import numpy as np, pandas as pd
a = pt.screen().adata
cs = pt.load('20261114T134310-C-states_and_composition-b254f4:cell_states').set_index('barcode')
o = a.obs.copy()
o['state'] = cs['state'].reindex(o.index).values
o['exp'] = np.where(o['unit'].str.startswith('NTN_2'),'NTN2',np.where(o['unit'].str.startswith('NTN_1'),'NTN1','Colitis'))
o = o[o['label_after_qc']!='failed QC']
groups = {'Th17core':['S01','S08','S02','S06'], 'cycling':['S11','S12','S17','S22'], 'clonalTCR_S14':['S14'], 'Treg_S20':['S20'], 'IFN':['S18','S19']}
for k,v in groups.items(): o[k]=o.state.isin(v)
ctrl=o[o.label_after_qc=='control']
out=[]
for e in ['NTN2','NTN1','Colitis']:
    c=ctrl[ctrl.exp==e]
    r={'target':'control','exp':e,'n':len(c)}
    for k in groups: r[k]=round(c[k].mean(),3)
    out.append(r)
    for t in sorted(o.label_after_qc.unique()):
        if t in ('control','none','multi','failed QC'): continue
        tt=o[(o.label_after_qc==t)&(o.exp==e)]
        if len(tt)<10: continue
        r={'target':t,'exp':e,'n':len(tt)}
        for k in groups: r[k]=round(tt[k].mean(),3)
        out.append(r)
G=pd.DataFrame(out)
pt.save_table('t9_group_shares', G)
pd.set_option('display.width',250); pd.set_option('display.max_rows',200)
print(G[G.exp=='NTN2'].to_string())
print(G[G.exp=='NTN1'].to_string())
print(G[G.exp=='Colitis'].to_string())
# Tgfbr1 NTN2 by unit
t=o[(o.label_after_qc=='Tgfbr1')&(o.exp=='NTN2')]
print(pd.crosstab(t.unit, t.state, normalize='index').round(2).to_string())
print(t.unit.value_counts())
print(pd.crosstab(t.guides, t.state).to_string())

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests
a = pt.screen().adata
o = a.obs.copy()
X = np.asarray(a.obsm['antibody_counts'].values, dtype=float)
gm = np.exp(np.log1p(X).mean(axis=1, keepdims=True))
CLR = np.log1p(X / gm)
prot = list(a.obsm['antibody_counts'].columns)
keep = o.label_after_qc.isin(['Tgfbr1','Rorc','Tbx21','control']).values
o = o[keep].copy(); CLR = CLR[keep]; o['row']=np.arange(len(o))
o['grp']=o.label_after_qc
o.to_pickle('/tmp/t8_obs.pkl') if False else None
def ols_test(y_mat, flag, units):
    # y_mat: n x p ; flag: bool n ; units: array of unit labels; design: intercept + unit dummies + flag
    U = pd.get_dummies(units, drop_first=True).values.astype(float)
    D = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(flag)), U, flag.astype(float)])
    XtX_inv = np.linalg.pinv(D.T @ D)
    B = XtX_inv @ D.T @ y_mat
    res = y_mat - D @ B
    dfres = D.shape[0]-D.shape[1]
    s2 = (res**2).sum(axis=0)/dfres
    se = np.sqrt(s2 * XtX_inv[-1,-1])
    beta = B[-1]
    from scipy import stats
    t = beta/se
    p = 2*stats.t.sf(np.abs(t), dfres)
    return beta, p
rows=[]
for cond in ['colitis','nephrotoxic_nephritis']:
    sub = o[o.condition==cond]
    yc = CLR[sub.row.values]
    units = sub.unit.values
    for tgt in ['Tgfbr1','Rorc','Tbx21']:
        flag = (sub.grp==tgt).values
        ctl = (sub.grp=='control').values
        m = flag|ctl
        beta,p = ols_test(yc[m], flag[m], units[m])
        mean_c = yc[m & ctl].mean(axis=0); mean_t = yc[m&flag].mean(axis=0)
        q = multipletests(p, method='fdr_bh')[1]
        for j,pr in enumerate(prot):
            rows.append(dict(condition=cond,target=tgt,score=pr,effect=beta[j],mean_diff=mean_t[j]-mean_c[j],p=p[j],q=q[j],n_t=flag[m].sum(),n_c=(ctl&m).sum()))
R = pd.DataFrame(rows)
R.to_csv('/tmp/t8_own_test.csv', index=False) if False else None
pt.save_table('t8_own_test', R)
print(R.groupby(['condition','target']).apply(lambda g: pd.Series({'n_q05':(g.q<0.05).sum(),'n_up':((g.q<0.05)&(g.effect>0)).sum(),'n_dn':((g.q<0.05)&(g.effect<0)).sum()})).to_string())

Why: set each target's composition shift beside the control-guide line within each experiment

Code
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
a = pt.screen().adata
cs = pt.load('20261114T134310-C-states_and_composition-b254f4:cell_states').set_index('barcode')
o = a.obs.copy()
o['state'] = cs['state'].reindex(o.index).values
o['exp'] = np.where(o['unit'].str.startswith('NTN_2'),'NTN2',np.where(o['unit'].str.startswith('NTN_1'),'NTN1','Colitis'))
o = o[(o['label_after_qc']!='failed QC') & o.state.notna()]
ctrl = o[o.label_after_qc=='control'].copy()
ctrl['cg'] = ctrl['control_group'].astype(str)
res=[]
for e in ['NTN2','NTN1','Colitis']:
    c = ctrl[ctrl.exp==e]
    states = sorted(o.state.unique())
    # null: each control group vs other controls in same exp
    groups = c.cg.value_counts()
    groups = groups[groups>=30].index.tolist()
    nulls=[]
    for g in groups:
        A = c[c.cg==g].state.value_counts(normalize=True).reindex(states, fill_value=0)
        B = c[c.cg!=g].state.value_counts(normalize=True).reindex(states, fill_value=0)
        nulls.append(0.5*np.abs(A-B).sum())
    ref = c.state.value_counts(normalize=True).reindex(states, fill_value=0)
    for t in sorted(o.label_after_qc.unique()):
        if t in ('control','none','multi','failed QC'): continue
        tt = o[(o.label_after_qc==t)&(o.exp==e)]
        if len(tt)<30: continue
        A = tt.state.value_counts(normalize=True).reindex(states, fill_value=0)
        tv = 0.5*np.abs(A-ref).sum()
        res.append(dict(exp=e,target=t,n=len(tt),TV=round(tv,3),ctrl_group_TV_median=round(np.median(nulls),3),ctrl_group_TV_max=round(np.max(nulls),3),n_ctrl_groups=len(groups)))
R=pd.DataFrame(res).sort_values(['exp','TV'],ascending=[True,False])
print(R.to_string())
# per guide Tgfbr1 NTN2 vs controls in NTN2 (TV and S14 share)
e='NTN2'
c=ctrl[ctrl.exp==e]; ref=c.state.value_counts(normalize=True)
for gname, sub in o[(o.label_after_qc=='Tgfbr1')&(o.exp==e)].groupby('guides'):
    if len(sub)<30: continue
    A=sub.state.value_counts(normalize=True).reindex(ref.index, fill_value=0)
    print(gname[:40], len(sub), 'TV', round(0.5*np.abs(A-ref.reindex(A.index,fill_value=0)).sum(),3), 'S14', round(A.get('S14',0),3))

o = o[(o['label_after_qc']!='failed QC') & o.state.notna()].copy()
o['grp'] = np.where(o.label_after_qc=='control','control', np.where(o.label_after_qc=='Tgfbr1', np.where(o.guides.astype(str).str.contains('Tgfbr1_1_capture'),'Tgfbr1_g1',np.where(o.guides.astype(str).str.contains('Tgfbr1_5_capture'),'Tgfbr1_g5','Tgfbr1_other')),'other'))
n2 = o[(o.exp=='NTN2')&o.grp.isin(['control','Tgfbr1_g1','Tgfbr1_g5'])].copy()
genes=['Trav6-1','Trbv3','Trbv2','Trav6-4','Il17a','Rorc','Ccr6','Il23r','Irf4','Il7r','Jak1','Tgfbr1','Il12rb2','Tbx21','Mki67','Ccnb2']
genes=[g for g in genes if g in a.var_names]
X = a[n2.index].X
Xd = X.toarray() if sp.issparse(X) else np.asarray(X)
D = pd.DataFrame(Xd, index=n2.index, columns=a.var_names)[genes]

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests
from scipy import stats
a = pt.screen().adata
o = a.obs.copy()
X = np.asarray(a.obsm['antibody_counts'].values, dtype=float)
gm = np.exp(np.log1p(X).mean(axis=1, keepdims=True))
CLR = np.log1p(X / gm)
prot = list(a.obsm['antibody_counts'].columns)
keep = o.label_after_qc.isin(['Tgfbr1','Rorc','Tbx21','control']).values
o = o[keep].copy(); CLR = CLR[keep]; o['row']=np.arange(len(o))
def ols_test(y_mat, flag, units):
    U = pd.get_dummies(units, drop_first=True).values.astype(float)
    D = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(flag)), U, flag.astype(float)])
    XtX_inv = np.linalg.pinv(D.T @ D)
    B = XtX_inv @ D.T @ y_mat
    res = y_mat - D @ B
    dfres = D.shape[0]-D.shape[1]
    s2 = (res**2).sum(axis=0)/dfres
    se = np.sqrt(s2 * XtX_inv[-1,-1])
    t = B[-1]/se
    return B[-1], 2*stats.t.sf(np.abs(t), dfres)
rows=[]
for cond in ['colitis','nephrotoxic_nephritis']:
    sub = o[(o.condition==cond)&(o.label_after_qc=='control')]
    cg = sub.control_group.values
    gl = sorted(set(cg), key=lambda s:int(s.split('_')[2]))
    assign = {g: i%3 for i,g in enumerate(gl)}
    yc = CLR[sub.row.values]; units=sub.unit.values
    for k in range(3):
        flag = np.array([assign[g]==k for g in cg])
        beta,p = ols_test(yc, flag, units)
        q = multipletests(p, method='fdr_bh')[1]
        for j,pr in enumerate(prot):
            rows.append(dict(condition=cond, group=f'ctrl_group{k}', score=pr, effect=beta[j], p=p[j], q=q[j], n=int(flag.sum())))
C = pd.DataFrame(rows)
pt.save_table('t8_control_line', C)
print(C.groupby(['condition','group']).apply(lambda g: pd.Series({'n_q05':(g.q<0.05).sum(),'max_abs_eff':g.effect.abs().max().round(3),'n':g.n.iloc[0]})).to_string())
print(C[C.q<0.05].assign(absE=lambda d: d.effect.abs()).sort_values('absE',ascending=False).head(12)[['condition','group','score','effect','q']].to_string())

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
pd.set_option('display.width',250)
a = pt.screen().adata
o = a.obs.copy()
X = np.asarray(a.obsm['antibody_counts'].values, dtype=float)
gm = np.exp(np.log1p(X).mean(axis=1, keepdims=True))
CLR = np.log1p(X / gm)
prot = list(a.obsm['antibody_counts'].columns)
keep = o.label_after_qc.isin(['Tgfbr1','Rorc','Tbx21','control']).values
o = o[keep].copy(); CLR = CLR[keep]; o['row']=np.arange(len(o))
picks = {'Rorc':['CD55_TotalSeqC','CD86_TotalSeqC','CD69_TotalSeqC','TCR-Vb8_1_TotalSeqC','CD38_TotalSeqC','CD49d_TotalSeqC','CD366_TotalSeqC'],
         'Tbx21':['CD55_TotalSeqC','Integrin-beta7_TotalSeqC','CD69_TotalSeqC','CD103_TotalSeqC','CD45_TotalSeqC','CD43_TotalSeqC'],
         'Tgfbr1':['TCR-Va2_TotalSeqC','CD45RB_TotalSeqC','CD49d_TotalSeqC','KLRG1_TotalSeqC','CD73_TotalSeqC','CD43_TotalSeqC']}
out=[]
for cond in ['colitis','nephrotoxic_nephritis']:
    sub=o[o.condition==cond]
    for tgt,pl in picks.items():
        for u in sorted(sub.unit.unique()):
            su = sub[sub.unit==u]
            if (su.label_after_qc==tgt).sum()<10 or (su.label_after_qc=='control').sum()<10: continue
            for pr in pl:
                j=prot.index(pr)
                t = CLR[su.row.values[su.label_after_qc==tgt], j].mean()
                c = CLR[su.row.values[su.label_after_qc=='control'], j].mean()
                out.append(dict(condition=cond,target=tgt,unit=u,protein=pr.replace('_TotalSeqC',''),diff=round(t-c,3),n_t=int((su.label_after_qc==tgt).sum()),n_c=int((su.label_after_qc=='control').sum())))
D=pd.DataFrame(out)
print(D.pivot_table(index=['condition','target','protein'],columns='unit',values='diff').to_string())
print(D.pivot_table(index=['condition','target'],columns='unit',values='n_t').to_string())

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests
from scipy import stats
pd.set_option('display.width',250)
a = pt.screen().adata
o0 = a.obs
print(o0[o0.unit=='NTN_2_23_1_Control'].label_after_qc.value_counts().head(8).to_string())
X = np.asarray(a.obsm['antibody_counts'].values, dtype=float)
gm = np.exp(np.log1p(X).mean(axis=1, keepdims=True))
CLR = np.log1p(X / gm)
prot = list(a.obsm['antibody_counts'].columns)
o = o0.copy(); o['row']=np.arange(len(o))
sel = o.label_after_qc.isin(['Tgfbr1','Rorc','Tbx21','control']) & (o.condition=='nephrotoxic_nephritis') & (o.unit.str.startswith('NTN_2_23_1'))
sub = o[sel]; yc = CLR[sub.row.values]; units = sub.unit.values
def ols_test(y_mat, flag, units):
    U = pd.get_dummies(units, drop_first=True).values.astype(float)
    D = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(flag)), U, flag.astype(float)])
    XtX_inv = np.linalg.pinv(D.T @ D)
    B = XtX_inv @ D.T @ y_mat
    res = y_mat - D @ B
    dfres = D.shape[0]-D.shape[1]
    s2 = (res**2).sum(axis=0)/dfres
    se = np.sqrt(s2 * XtX_inv[-1,-1])
    return B[-1], 2*stats.t.sf(np.abs(B[-1]/se), dfres)
rows=[]
lab = sub.label_after_qc.values
ctl = lab=='control'
print('ctrl cells', ctl.sum(), 'units', pd.Series(units[ctl]).value_counts().to_dict())
for tgt in ['Tgfbr1','Rorc','Tbx21']:
    flag = lab==tgt; m = flag|ctl
    beta,p = ols_test(yc[m], flag[m], units[m])
    q = multipletests(p, method='fdr_bh')[1]
    for j,pr in enumerate(prot):
        rows.append(dict(condition='nephrotoxic_nephritis (protein units)', target=tgt, score=pr, effect=beta[j], q=q[j], n_t=int(flag.sum()), n_c=int(ctl.sum())))
R2 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
# control line on the same units
cg = sub.control_group.values
cmask = ctl
gl = sorted(set(cg[cmask]), key=lambda s:int(s.split('_')[2]))
assign = {g:i%3 for i,g in enumerate(gl)}
crow=[]
for k in range(3):
    flag = np.array([assign.get(g,-1)==k for g in cg]) & cmask
    m = cmask
    beta,p = ols_test(yc[m], flag[m], units[m])
    q = multipletests(p, method='fdr_bh')[1]
    crow.append(dict(group=k, n_q05=int((q<0.05).sum()), max_abs=float(np.abs(beta).max()), n=int(flag.sum())))
print(pd.DataFrame(R2).groupby('target').apply(lambda g: pd.Series({'n_q05':(g.q<0.05).sum(),'max_abs':g.effect.abs().max()})).round(3))
print(pd.DataFrame(crow))
pt.save_table('t8_ntn_protein_units', R2)

def ols_flag(y, flag, units):
    U = pd.get_dummies(units, drop_first=True).values.astype(float)
    D = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(flag)), U, flag.astype(float)])
    XtX_inv = np.linalg.pinv(D.T @ D)
    B = XtX_inv @ D.T @ y
    res = y - D @ B
    dfres = D.shape[0]-D.shape[1]
    s2 = (res**2).sum(axis=0)/dfres
    se = np.sqrt(s2 * XtX_inv[-1,-1])
    return B[-1], 2*stats.t.sf(np.abs(B[-1]/se), dfres)
for cond in ['colitis','nephrotoxic_nephritis']:
    s = G[G.condition==cond]
    for tgt in ['Tgfbr1','Rorc','Tbx21']:
        m = s.label_after_qc.isin([tgt,'control']).values
        flag = (s.label_after_qc==tgt).values[m]
        y = s[present].values[m]
        beta,p = ols_flag(y, flag, s.unit.values[m])
        for j,g in enumerate(present):
            rows.append(dict(condition=cond,target=tgt,gene=g,rna_effect=beta[j],rna_p=p[j]))
RN = pd.DataFrame(rows)

        print(cond,tgt)

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
from scipy import stats
a = pt.screen().adata
o = a.obs.copy(); o['row']=np.arange(len(o))
gmap = {'CD4':'Cd4','CD8a':'Cd8a','CD366':'Havcr2','PD-1':'Pdcd1','Ly-6C':'Ly6c1','CD11b':'Itgam','Ly-6G':'Ly6g','CD49f':'Itga6','CD44':'Cd44','CD54':'Icam1','CD90_2':'Thy1','CD73':'Nt5e','CD49d':'Itga4','CD200':'Cd200','CD45':'Ptprc','CD45RB':'Ptprc','CD45_2':'Ptprc','CD25':'Il2ra','CD11c':'Itgax','CD43':'Spn','CD5':'Cd5','CD62L':'Sell','CD93':'Cd93','KLRG1':'Klrg1','CD3':'Cd3e','ICOS':'Icos','PD-L1':'Cd274','CD27':'Cd27','CD357':'Tnfrsf18','CD137':'Tnfrsf9','CD134':'Tnfrsf4','CD69':'Cd69','IL-7RA':'Il7r','CD86':'Cd86','CD103':'Itgae','CD150':'Slamf1','Integrin-beta7':'Itgb7','CXCR3':'Cxcr3','CD49b':'Itga2','CD226':'Cd226','CXCR6':'Cxcr6','Ly108':'Slamf6','CD98':'Slc3a2','CD94':'Klrd1','CD29':'Itgb1','CD38':'Cd38','CD55':'Cd55','CD48':'Cd48','CCR6':'Ccr6','CD61':'Itgb3','CD51':'Itgav','CD223':'Lag3','CD272':'Btla','CD2':'Cd2','CD71':'Tfrc','Ly-6A_E':'Ly6a','CD160':'Cd160','CD9':'Cd9','CD81':'Cd81','TCR-b-chain':'Trbc1','CD8b':'Cd8b1','CD106':'Vcam1','CD24':'Cd24a','CD63':'Cd63','CD107a':'Lamp1'}
prot = list(a.obsm['antibody_counts'].columns)
X = np.asarray(a.obsm['antibody_counts'].values, dtype=float)
CLR = np.log1p(X / np.exp(np.log1p(X).mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)))
present = sorted(set(gmap.values()))
ci = {g:i for i,g in enumerate(a.var_names)}
LN = pt.screen().lognorm
def ols_flag(y, flag, units):
    U = pd.get_dummies(units, drop_first=True).values.astype(float)
    D = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(flag)), U, flag.astype(float)])
    XtX_inv = np.linalg.pinv(D.T @ D); B = XtX_inv @ D.T @ y
    res = y - D @ B; dfres = D.shape[0]-D.shape[1]
    s2 = (res**2).sum(axis=0)/dfres
    return B[-1]
out=[]
pm = [p for p in prot if p.replace('_TotalSeqC','') in gmap]
for cond in ['colitis','nephrotoxic_nephritis']:
    base = o[(o.condition==cond)&(o.label_after_qc.isin(['control','Tgfbr1','Rorc','Tbx21']))].copy()
    if cond=='nephrotoxic_nephritis':
        base = base[base.unit.str.startswith('NTN_2_23_1')]
    ctl = base[base.label_after_qc=='control']
    gl = sorted(set(ctl.control_group), key=lambda s:int(s.split('_')[2]))
    assign = {g:i%3 for i,g in enumerate(gl)}
    G = LN[base.row.values][:, [ci[g] for g in present]].toarray()
    Gd = pd.DataFrame(G, columns=present)
    Pd = pd.DataFrame(CLR[base.row.values], columns=prot)
    for k in range(3):
        flag_all = np.array([(assign.get(g,-1)==k) for g in base.control_group]) & (base.label_after_qc=='control').values
        m = (base.label_after_qc=='control').values
        flag = flag_all[m]
        bp = ols_flag(Pd[pm].values[m], flag, base.unit.values[m])
        br = ols_flag(Gd.values[m], flag, base.unit.values[m])
        pe = dict(zip(pm,bp)); re_ = dict(zip(present,br))
        pairs = [(pe[p], re_[gmap[p.replace('_TotalSeqC','')]]) for p in pm if p.replace('_TotalSeqC','') in gmap]
        pa = np.array(pairs)
        rho,pv = stats.spearmanr(pa[:,0], pa[:,1])
        out.append(dict(condition=cond, pseudo_group=k, n_cells=int(flag.sum()), spearman=round(rho,3), n_pairs=len(pa)))
print(pd.DataFrame(out).to_string())

import numpy as np, pandas as pd, scipy.sparse as sp
a = pt.screen().adata; o = a.obs
vn = np.array(a.var_names)
trb = np.array([i for i,v in enumerate(vn) if v.startswith('Trbv')])
o2 = o.copy(); o2['guide']=o2.guides.astype(str).str.extract(r'(gRNA_[A-Za-z0-9]+_\d)')[0]
ntn2 = o2.unit.str.startswith('NTN_2').values
def prof(mask):
    X = a[mask][:, trb].X
    X = X.tocsr() if sp.issparse(X) else sp.csr_matrix(X)
    has = np.asarray(X.sum(1)).ravel()>0
    dom = np.asarray(X.argmax(1)).ravel()[has]
    s = pd.Series(vn[trb][dom]).value_counts(normalize=True)
    return has.sum(), s.head(4).round(2).to_dict()
for name,m in [('Tgfbr1 g1 NTN2', ntn2&(o2.guide=='gRNA_Tgfbr1_1').values&(o2.label_after_qc=='Tgfbr1').values),
               ('control NTN2', ntn2&(o2.label_after_qc=='control').values),
               ('Tgfbr1 other guides NTN2', ntn2&(o2.guide!='gRNA_Tgfbr1_1').values&(o2.label_after_qc=='Tgfbr1').values),
               ('Rorc NTN2', ntn2&(o2.label_after_qc=='Rorc').values),
               ('Tgfbr1 g1 NTN1+colitis', (~ntn2)&(o2.guide=='gRNA_Tgfbr1_1').values&(o2.label_after_qc=='Tgfbr1').values)]:
    print(name, prof(m))

import numpy as np, pandas as pd
ad = pt.screen().adata
cs = pt.load("20261114T142946-C-states_and_composition-20a03f:cell_states")
cs = cs.set_index('barcode')
ad.obs['state'] = cs['state'].reindex(ad.obs_names).values
genes = ['Il17a','Il23r','Ccr6','Ifng','Cxcr3','Rorc','Tbx21','Il17f','Il1r1']
genes = [g for g in genes if g in ad.var_names]
X = ad[:, genes].X
import scipy.sparse as sp
X = X.toarray() if sp.issparse(X) else np.asarray(X)
lib = np.asarray(ad.X.sum(axis=1)).ravel()
lg = np.log1p(X / lib[:,None] * 1e4)
df = pd.DataFrame(lg, columns=genes, index=ad.obs_names)
df['label'] = ad.obs['label_after_qc'].values
df['state'] = ad.obs['state'].values
df['unit'] = ad.obs['unit'].values
df['ctrl'] = ad.obs['control_kind'].values
for s in ['S02','S06','S07','S11']:
    sub = df[df.state==s]
    ctrl = sub[sub.label=='control']
    out = {}
    for t in ['Rorc','Tbx21']:
        tc = sub[sub.label==t]
        out[t+'_n'] = len(tc)
        for g in ['Il17a','Il23r','Ccr6','Ifng','Cxcr3']:
            out[t+'_'+g] = round(tc[g].mean()-ctrl[g].mean(),2)
    out['ctrl_n'] = len(ctrl)
    print(s, out)

Why: Answer d-f3-wording: is the lower Il17a/Ccr6/Rorc present without guide 1?

Code
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import mannwhitneyu
a = pt.screen().adata
o = a.obs.copy()
g = o['guides'].astype(str)
o['guide'] = g.str.extract(r'(gRNA_[A-Za-z0-9]+_\d)')[0]
single = ~g.str.contains(';')
ctrl = o['control_kind'].astype(str)=='non_targeting'
o['grp'] = np.where(o['guide']=='gRNA_Tgfbr1_1','g1', np.where(o['guide'].astype(str).str.startswith('gRNA_Tgfbr1'),'other_Tgfbr1', np.where(ctrl,'control','x')))
ntn2 = o['sample'].astype(str).str.startswith('NTN_2')
sel = single & ntn2 & o['grp'].isin(['g1','other_Tgfbr1','control'])
sub = a[sel.values]
tot = np.asarray(sub.X.sum(1)).ravel()
res=[]
for gene in ['Il17a','Ccr6','Rorc','Tgfbr1']:
    x = sub[:, gene].X
    x = np.asarray(x.todense()).ravel() if hasattr(x,'todense') else np.asarray(x).ravel()
    v = np.log1p(x/tot*1e4)
    d = pd.DataFrame({'v':v,'grp':o.loc[sel,'grp'].values})
    m = d.groupby('grp')['v'].mean()
    for t in ['g1','other_Tgfbr1']:
        p = mannwhitneyu(d.v[d.grp==t], d.v[d.grp=='control']).pvalue
        res.append((gene,t,(d.grp==t).sum(),round(m[t]-m['control'],3),p))
print(pd.DataFrame(res,columns=['gene','group','cells','mean_logCP10k_diff_vs_control','p']).to_string())

['figures']
"""A finding's figure as published screens build it (docs/build/adr0022/07_figure_series_from_papers.md): several
panels, each a chart of charts.py or one's own drawing, in its part of one figure 183 mm wide, lettered a, b, c in
reading order, laid out together and checked as one figure (figures.check_figure).

A figure is given as rows: [(height in mm, [(width share, draw), ...]), ...], where draw(panel) draws into the panel
(a matplotlib subfigure): a chart, for example lambda p: charts.volcano(table, None, "", fig=p), or one's own code,
for example lambda p: p.add_subplot().plot(x, y). A panel may carry its title, what it shows in a short sentence:
(width share, draw, title).
"""
import os
import string
import textwrap

from . import figures

LETTER_PT = 8
TITLE_PT = 6


def _letter_and_title(sf, letter, title, width):
    """A panel's letter, bold at its top left, and its title beside it, wrapped to the panel's width (inches). The
    layout keeps room above the panel for a subfigure's title only when the title's height is left to it (no y), so
    the letter, or the title with the letter beside it, is that title."""
    if not title:
        sf.suptitle(letter, x=0.0, ha="left", fontsize=LETTER_PT, fontweight="bold")
        return
    from matplotlib.transforms import ScaledTranslation
    indent = 1.6 * LETTER_PT / 72  # inches: the letter and a space
    chars = max(12, int((width - indent) * 72 / (0.5 * TITLE_PT)))  # about half the font size per character
    t = sf.suptitle(textwrap.fill(str(title), chars), x=0.0, ha="left", fontsize=TITLE_PT)
    t.set_transform(sf.transSubfigure + ScaledTranslation(indent, 0, sf.figure.dpi_scale_trans))
    sf.text(0.0, 1.0, letter, transform=sf.transSubfigure, ha="left", va="top", fontsize=LETTER_PT,
            fontweight="bold")


def figure(rows, width=figures.DOUBLE):
    """The rows of panels drawn into one figure, lettered and laid out; returns the figure and the panels' letters in
    order. Nothing is saved: in a notebook, save_figure(fig, name, data, caption, role, strict=True) enters it in the
    record; a module's figure is saved by compose."""
    plt = figures._plt()
    height = sum(h for h, _ in rows) * figures.MM
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(width, height), layout="constrained")
    fig.get_layout_engine().set(w_pad=1.5 / 72, h_pad=1.5 / 72, wspace=0.02, hspace=0.02)
    row_figs = fig.subfigures(len(rows), 1, height_ratios=[h for h, _ in rows], squeeze=False)[:, 0]
    letters, k = [], 0
    for rf, (_, panels) in zip(row_figs, rows):
        shares = [p[0] for p in panels]
        subs = rf.subfigures(1, len(panels), width_ratios=shares, squeeze=False)[0]
        for sf, (share, draw, *title) in zip(subs, panels):
            letter = string.ascii_lowercase[k]
            k += 1
            draw(sf)
            _letter_and_title(sf, letter, title[0] if title else None, width * share / sum(shares))
            letters.append(letter)
    fig.canvas.draw()  # the layout

def figure(rows, width=figures.DOUBLE):; """The rows of panels drawn into one figure, lettered and laid out; returns the figure and the panels' letters in; order. Nothing is saved: in a notebook, save_figure(fig, name, data, caption, role, ...

Why: Need the panel signature to draw

Code
import pertura.question_modules.figure_series as fs, inspect
print(inspect.getsource(fs.figure)[:3000])
print(inspect.getsource(fs.compose)[:1500])
import pertura.question_modules.charts as ch

Output
def figure(rows, width=figures.DOUBLE):
    """The rows of panels drawn into one figure, lettered and laid out; returns the figure and the panels' letters in
    order. Nothing is saved: in a notebook, save_figure(fig, name, data, caption, role, strict=True) enters it in the
    record; a module's figure is saved by compose."""
    plt = figures._plt()
    height = sum(h for h, _ in rows) * figures.MM
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(width, height), layout="constrained")
    fig.get_layout_engine().set(w_pad=1.5 / 72, h_pad=1.5 / 72, wspace=0.02, hspace=0.02)
    row_figs = fig.subfigures(len(rows), 1, height_ratios=[h for h, _ in rows], squeeze=False)[:, 0]
    letters, k = [], 0
    for rf, (_, panels) in zip(row_figs, rows):
        shares = [p[0] for p in panels]
        subs = rf.subfigures(1, len(panels), width_ratios=shares, squeeze=False)[0]
        for sf, (share, draw, *title) in zip(subs, panels):
            letter = string.ascii_lowercase[k]
            k += 1
            draw(sf)
            _letter_and_title(sf, letter, title[0] if title else None, width * share / sum(shares))
            letters.append(letter)
    fig.canvas.draw()  # the layout is final: the panels' labels are placed now (charts._after_layout)
    for place in fig.__dict__.pop("_after_layout", []):
        place()
    return fig, letters

def compose(rows, path, title, width=figures.DOUBLE):
    """Draws the rows of panels into one figure, letters them, and saves it; returns the layout checks' issues (empty
    when none) and the panels' letters in order."""
    plt = figures._plt()
    fig, letters = figure(rows, width)
    issues = figures.check_figure(fig)
    fig.savefig(path, metadata={"Title": title}, dpi=300)
    fig.savefig(os.path.splitext(path)[0] + ".pdf", metadata={"Title": title})
    plt.close(fig)
    return issues, letters

Output
heatmap (M, rows, cols, path, title, label, marks=None, cluster=True, width=None, cap=None, fig=None)
A matrix (rows x cols) on a diverging scale centred on zero, rows and columns clustered; marks: the same
    shape, a significance mark per cell (strings), drawn as a dot where the columns are too narrow for text
    (MARKS_AS_DOTS); cap: a percentile of the absolute values at which the scale stops (the colour bar's ends then
    mark that larger values exist), so a few extreme values do not wash 
---
strips (table, value, group, path, xlabel, title='', order=None, log=False, fig=None, points_at_most=None, xlim=None)
A value's spread in each group (table: group, value), a box per group with every item a point, the number of
    items in the group's label: cells per guide for the targeting and the control guides, for example. With
    points_at_most, a larger group shows that many points drawn at random; its box holds every item. xlim: the
    axis's range where the value has one (a share, 0 to 1).
---
ranked_targets (table, value, path, ylabel, title, q=None, control_band=None, top=80, control_line=None, muted=None, own_line=None, fig=None)
All targets ranked by `value` (table: target, value, and q if given): one bar each, significance marks above,
    the control guides' range as a grey band (control_band: (low, high)) or a dashed line at zero; control_line:
    (value, its name in the key), a dotted line such as the control-guide groups' 95th percentile; muted: (targets,
    their name in the key), drawn in light grey (a reading th
---
target_panel (C, side, path=None, title='The targets', label='Correlation of profiles', fig=None, order=None, boxes=())
The targets in one panel, as Belk et al. 2022 draw them: the correlation of every two targets' profiles (C,
    a square table; missing values grey), clustered, with a column of bars beside it for each measure in side (a
    table indexed by target: cells, genes changed, a score), signed measures red above zero and blue below. order:
    the targets' order, where a clustering of its own gives it; 
---
diverging_colour_bar (fig, im, label, capped=False, **where)
A colour bar for a scale centred on zero: a few ticks set symmetrically about zero, the label wrapped to two
    lines where it is long, so neither runs past the bar.
---
knockdown_vs_baseline (table, path, title, label_top=8, fig=None)
Each guide's knockdown of its target gene against the gene's baseline expression in the control cells (table:
    guide, baseline, log2fc, and past_the_line if given): a guide short of the line drawn hollow.
---
pair_correlations (pairs, path, title, fig=None)
Two guides' profile correlations by kind of pair (pairs: kind, correlation): a box per kind with every pair
    drawn as a point, and the number of pairs in its label, so a reference of few pairs shows as few (as Akana et al.
    2026 and Belk et al. 2022 compare guides of one gene with other pairs).

def heatmap(M, rows, cols, path, title, label, marks=None, cluster=True, width=None, cap=None, fig=None):
    """A matrix (rows x cols) on a diverging scale centred on zero, rows and columns clustered; marks: the same
    shape, a significance mark per cell (strings), drawn as a dot where the columns are too narrow for text
    (MARKS_AS_DOTS); cap: a percentile of the absolute values at which the scale stops (the colour bar's ends then
    mark that larger values exist), so a few extreme values do not wash out the rest."""
    plt = figures._plt()
    M = np.asarray(M, float)
    r, c = _order(M) if cluster else (np.arange(M.shape[0]), np.arange(M.shape[1]))
    M = M[r][:, c]
    rows, cols = [rows[i] for i in r], [cols[j] for j in c]
    lim = float(np.nanmax(np.abs(M))) if np.isfinite(M).any() else 1.0
    capped = False
    if cap is not None and np.isfinite(M).any():
        at = float(np.nanpercentile(np.abs(M[np.abs(M) > 0]), cap)) if (np.abs(M) > 0).any() else lim
        capped, lim = at < lim, min(lim, at) or lim
    w = width or (DOUBLE if len(cols) > 18 else SINGLE)
    fig, own = _canvas(plt, fig, (w, _height(len(rows))), layout="constrained")
    ax = fig.add_subplot()
    im = ax.imshow(M, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-lim, vmax=lim, aspect="auto", interpolation="nearest")
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(cols)))
    ax.set_xticklabels([figures.short_name(x) for x in cols], rotation=90, fontsize=5 if len(cols) > 30 else 6)
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(rows)))
    ax.set_yticklabels(rows, fontsize=5 if len(rows) > 30 else 6)
    if marks is not None:
        mk = np.asarray(marks, dtype=object)[r][:, c]
        dark = np.abs(np.nan_to_num(M)) > 0.6 * (lim or 1.0)  # a mark on a dark cell is white
        where = [(i, j) for i in range(mk.shape[0]) for j in range(mk.shape[1]) if mk[i, j]]
        if mk.shape[1] > MARKS_AS_DOTS:
            if where:
                ax.scatter([j for _, j in where], [i for i, _ in where], s=1.5, linewidths=0, zorder=3,
                           c=["white" if dark[i, j] else "black" for i, j in where])
        else:
            for i, j in where:
                ax.text(j, i, mk[i, j], ha="center", va="center", fontsize=5,
                        color="white" if dark[i, j] else "black")
    diverging_colour_bar(fig, im, label, capped, ax=ax, fraction=0.04, pad=0.02)
    return _done(plt, fig, own, path, title)

def stars(q):
    """Significance marks: *** below 0.001, ** below 0.01, * below 0.05."""
    return "***" if q < 0.001 else "**" if q < 0.01 else "*" if q < 0.05 else ""

                   muted=None, own_line=None, fig=None):
    """All targets ranked by `value

import numpy as np, pandas as pd, re
a = pt.screen().adata
obs = a.obs.copy()
gl = obs['guides'].astype(str)
print(gl.head(3).tolist(), gl[gl.str.contains(';|,')].head(3).tolist())
allg = gl.apply(lambda s: sorted(set(re.findall(r'gRNA_[A-Za-z0-9]+_\d', s))))
obs['nguides'] = allg.apply(len)
obs['guide'] = allg.apply(lambda l: l[0] if len(l)==1 else None)
trbv = [i for i,v in enumerate(a.var_names) if v.startswith('Trbv')]
X = a.X[:, trbv]
X = X.toarray() if hasattr(X,'toarray') else np.asarray(X)
tot = X.sum(1)
dom = np.array([a.var_names[trbv[j]] for j in X.argmax(1)])
obs['dom'] = dom
obs['trbv_tot'] = tot
sub = obs[(obs.nguides==1) & (obs.trbv_tot>0) & (obs.qc_reason.astype(str)=='')]
sub = sub.assign(grp=np.where(sub.guide=='gRNA_Tgfbr1_1','Tgfbr1 guide 1',
      np.where(sub.guide.fillna('').str.startswith('gRNA_Tgfbr1_'),'Tgfbr1 other guides',
      np.where(sub.control_kind=='non_targeting','controls',None))))
sub = sub[sub.grp.notna()]
sub = sub.assign(is_trbv3=(sub.dom=='Trbv3'))
tab = sub.groupby(['unit','grp']).agg(share=('is_trbv3','mean'), n=('is_trbv3','size')).reset_index()
print(tab.to_string())
print(sub.guide.unique()[:0], sorted(sub.guide.dropna().unique())[:0])
print(obs[obs.guide.fillna('').str.startswith('gRNA_Tgfbr1')].groupby('guide').size())
pt.save_table('fig3_panel_a_trbv3_share', tab)

obs['guide'] = allg.apply(lambda l: l[0] if len(l)==1 else None)
trbv = [i for i,v in enumerate(a.var_names) if v.startswith('Trbv')]

tabA = pt.load('table:fig3_panel_a_trbv3_share').copy()
units_order = ['NTN_2_23_1_Th17-1','NTN_2_23_1_Th17-2','NTN_2_23_1_Th17-3','NTN_1_19_23_1','NTN_1_19_23_2','NTN_1_19_5','NTN_1_19_9_1','NTN_1_19_9_2','Colitis_2_23_2_Th17-1','Colitis_2_23_2_Th17-2']
tabA = tabA[tabA.unit.isin(units_order)]
tabA['x'] = tabA.unit.map({u:i for i,u in enumerate(units_order)})
tabB = pd.DataFrame({
 'guide':['gRNA_Tgfbr1_1','gRNA_Tgfbr1_2','gRNA_Tgfbr1_3','gRNA_Tgfbr1_4','gRNA_Tgfbr1_5'],
 'own_gene_log2fc':[-0.0683,-1.3164,-0.8348,-0.6903,0.3945],
 'cells':[2788,107,527,107,255],
 'measurable':[True,False,True,False,True],
 'verdict':['transcript unchanged','not measurable','at least 30% down','not measurable','transcript unchanged']})
tabB['y'] = range(len(tabB))[::-1]
pt.save_table('fig3_panel_b_own_gene', tabB)
C_G1, C_OTH, C_CTL = '#B2182B', '#2166AC', '#9E9E9E'
def drawA(p):
    ax = p.add_subplot()
    off = {'Tgfbr1 guide 1':-0.22,'Tgfbr1 other guides':0.0,'controls':0.22}
    col = {'Tgfbr1 guide 1':C_G1,'Tgfbr1 other guides':C_OTH,'controls':C_CTL}
    for g in off:
        d = tabA[tabA.grp==g]

Generated from the modules

Analyses

Each tool the agent calls, with its analyses. The package functions and the example figures come from runs on synthetic screens. Each analysis has its entry in the knowledge base.

guides

Guide calls and their evidence, cells per target, each target's own gene, escape (Mixscape or Mixscale), dose, clones, the vectors' structure, and the controls that cut against those that do not

The evidence behind each cell's guide call · calls

The evidence for each cell's guide call.

Applies to: always

Each target's cells against the control guides' · cells

Each target's cell count against the control guides'.

Applies to: always (read against the library's representation when there is one)

Calls: MAGeCK: test

Each guide's change of its own target gene · own_gene

Each guide's change of its own target gene, described against a line.

Applies to: a modality acting on the target gene (CRISPRi, CRISPRa, knockout)

Perturbed and non-perturbed cells within a target's cells · escape

Within a target's cells, some cells were changed by the perturbation and some were not (mosaic editing, in-frame edits, weak knockdown in some cells).

Applies to: CRISPRi or knockout

Calls: pertpy: tl.Mixscape.perturbation_signature, tl.Mixscape.mixscape; scanpy: pp.highly_variable_genes, pp.pca

How much a target's guides differ in efficacy · dose

A target's guides can differ in efficacy, so pooling them averages over their efficacies (G4, PF8).

Applies to: CRISPRi or CRISPRa

Expanded clones among a guide's cells · clones

A guide's cells can descend from a few transduced cells that expanded.

Applies to: in vivo

Guides that travel on one vector · vectors

Some libraries put a target's guides on one vector (dual-guide vectors, arrays).

Applies to: vectors of two or more guides, or two guides per cell by design

The response to cutting DNA · cutting

The response to cutting itself: the cells of control guides that cut where no gene is (intergenic, safe-targeting) against the non-targeting ones.

Applies to: control guides that target DNA where no gene is (intergenic, safe-targeting) beside non-targeting ones, under any modality

impact

Which targets change the cells, and how much, against the controls; the response many targets share

Each target's effect on the whole profile · distance

A target's effect on the cells' whole profile.

Applies to: always

Calls: pertpy: tl.DistanceTest; scanpy: pp.highly_variable_genes, pp.pca; statsmodels: stats.multitest.multipletests

A target's effect beyond the response all perturbations share · shared

The part of a target's effect that remains once the response every perturbation shares is set aside.

Applies to: 3 or more targets

Calls: pertpy: tl.DistanceTest; scanpy: pp.highly_variable_genes, pp.pca; statsmodels: stats.multitest.multipletests

genes

The genes each target changes; named genes read across the targets (genes); the targets' network (genes targets_own)

The genes each target changes · genes

Most published screens test a target's cells against the control cells, most often with a Wilcoxon test; fewer sum the cells by replicate (pseudobulk).

Applies to: always

Calls: Seurat: FindMarkers; edgeR: glmQLFit, glmQLFTest; pertura: a rank test within each sample (its own code, until the module is converted); scanpy: tl.rank_genes_groups

scores

Each target's effect on per-cell scores: an MSigDB collection (gene_sets, select), lists of your own (gene_lists), the control cells' contrast between two levels (contrast), the proteins (gene_sets proteins), or any per-cell value (cell_values)

The gene programs each target moves · scores

Coordinated gene programs, and each target's effect on each.

Applies to: always

Calls: cnmf: cNMF prepare, factorize, combine, consensus; scanpy: tl.rank_genes_groups; scanpy: tl.score_genes; scikit-learn: decomposition.NMF; scipy: stats.ranksums; statsmodels: OLS; statsmodels: stats.multitest.multipletests

states

Cell states with their naming evidence and each target's shares of them; changes within a state; the cell cycle; a trajectory (trajectory_root)

Cell states, and each target's share of them · states

Cell states found without the perturbation labels (Leiden clusters named by their markers), and each target's share of cells in each state against the control cells.

Applies to: always

Calls: scanpy: pp.normalize_total, pp.log1p, pp.highly_variable_genes, pp.scale, tl.pca, pp.neighbors, tl.leiden, tl.umap, tl.rank_genes_groups; scipy: stats.fisher_exact; speckle: getTransformedProps, propeller.ttest; statsmodels: stats.multitest.multipletests

Changes within a state, beside shifts between states · within

It tells a target that moves cells between states from one that changes cells within a state.

Applies to: a target whose share of a state shifted (C.states_and_composition)

Calls: scanpy: tl.rank_genes_groups

Each target's cell-cycle phases · cell_cycle

Each cell's phase from the S and G2/M genes (Tirosh et al.

Applies to: human or mouse (experiment.organism)

Calls: scanpy: tl.score_genes_cell_cycle; scipy: stats.fisher_exact; statsmodels: stats.multitest.multipletests

programs

Gene programmes found in the cells (cNMF, unless choices gene_sets names another method), with each target's usage

The gene programs each target moves · programs

Coordinated gene programs, and each target's effect on each.

Applies to: always

Calls: cnmf: cNMF prepare, factorize, combine, consensus; scanpy: tl.rank_genes_groups; scanpy: tl.score_genes; scikit-learn: decomposition.NMF; scipy: stats.ranksums; statsmodels: OLS; statsmodels: stats.multitest.multipletests

similarity

Targets alike or opposite, the genes they share and their complexes; sets of targets that act together; the regulators along a programme's axis

Targets with similar profiles · alike

Perturbations of one complex or pathway look alike, so an unknown gene can be placed by the known ones it resembles.

Applies to: 3 or more targets

Calls: numpy: profiles compared (pearson), each cell against its sample's control cells

Regulators of one program that act together · sets

The regulators of one program, clustered by what else they move into sets that act together.

Applies to: the regulators of one program (C.programs), and their effects on the others

Two programs the regulators move together or apart · axis

Two programs that the regulators move in opposite (or the same) directions: an axis of the cell's regulation.

Applies to: each target's effect on several programs (C.programs)

conditions

Effects across conditions, time points, cell types or modes (what: the controls' own response, genes, scores or shares; pair: the two conditions)

Effects that differ between conditions · conditions

A perturbation's effect compared between conditions (a stimulus, a time point, a tissue, a cell type).

Applies to: 2 or more conditions

Activation against inhibition of one gene · modes

CRISPRa and CRISPRi of one gene in one library.

Applies to: CRISPRa and CRISPRi of the same genes in one library

combinations

Pairs of perturbations against their singles

Each pair against its singles · pairs

Two perturbations together against each alone.

Applies to: pairs or sets

Calls: numpy: linalg.lstsq (Norman et al. 2019's fit of a pair on its singles)

enrichment

What changed genes mean: gene sets in each target's changed genes from a genes run (de; up and down apart, or method gsea on its ranking) or in a list; the activity of factors and pathways (method ulm with collection collectri or progeny, on a genes run: de); a factor's direct targets

The gene sets a finding's genes fall in · meaning

The meaning of a finding's changed genes: the gene sets they over-represent (up and down apart, against the genes the screen detects), or where a ranking enriches (GSEA).

Applies to: always

Calls: gseapy: enrich

A factor's known targets, as its perturbation moves them · direct_targets

For a perturbed transcription factor, the way its known targets (CollecTRI's regulons) move, against what its regulon and the perturbation predict.

Applies to: a perturbed regulator (a transcription factor) whose changed genes were measured

Calls: decoupler: mt.ulm

reproducibility

Whether a result holds: the guides of a target agree, the replicates agree, the calls hold with fewer cells

Agreement between a target's guides · guides

The agreement of a target's guides, beyond what two control guides share.

Applies to: 2 or more guides per target

Calls: numpy: profiles compared (pearson), each cell against its sample's control cells

Agreement between samples · replicates

The agreement of the units (mice, donors, captures) on the targets' profiles.

Applies to: 2 or more samples or lanes

Calls: numpy: corrcoef (Pearson) of profiles, replicate against replicate

Each target's effect on the whole profile · fewer_cells

A target's effect on the cells' whole profile.

Applies to: always

Calls: pertpy: tl.DistanceTest; scanpy: pp.highly_variable_genes, pp.pca; statsmodels: stats.multitest.multipletests

The first look, run by code

The screen at a glance

Every target side by side, before any one is followed.

Applies to: after the first look: every target by every kind of evidence its runs measured

Calls: pertpy: tl.Distance; scanpy: pp.highly_variable_genes, pp.pca

The cells the experiment holds, by unit and kind

This module counts the cells of the experiment per unit (capture, mouse, donor): cells with one target, with two or more, with a control guide, with an ambiguous call, and with no call.

Applies to: always
